subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A bad patch

options.text: A period of time when a person faces lots of troubles
A person who takes a difficult path
A dangerous road to walk on

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"A bad patch"** means a period of time when a person faces lots of troubles. (कठिन समय)

 
 
• **Example:** After losing his job, John went through a bad patch where nothing seemed to go right.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** A path that is unravelled (एक रास्ता जो खुल गया है)

 
 
• **Example:** The hiker found himself on an unravelled path in the dense forest.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** A person who takes a difficult path (एक व्यक्ति जो कठिन रास्ता अपनाता है)
 
 
• **Example:** She is known as someone who always takes the difficult path to achieve her goals.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** A dangerous road to walk on (चलने के लिए एक खतरनाक सड़क)
 
 
• **Example:** The old bridge has become a dangerous road to walk on due to years of neglect.
